title: Make a polished commercial fast
summary: A fast route from brief to a finished 30-60 second commercial, product spot or brand ad, with generation, voice, finishing, and publishing covered.
best_for: Launch videos, UGC-style ads, app promos, product drops, and quick brand spots for a campaign.
martini_handoff: Use Martini as the production workspace when the agent and the team need to work the same shots — generation across models, client comments, approvals, and spend per shot — instead of juggling one-off tools.

primary.why: Keeps shots, takes, approvals, and spend on one canvas and timeline that the team and the agent share, over MCP, CLI, or API.
Strong direct fit for captioned product, app-demo, lip-synced, and social-ready UGC videos.
Hosted first-party video generation for hero shots and polished model output.
Voiceover, voice design, sound effects, music, and dialogue isolation in one official audio server.
Agent-native Mac timeline editing for assembly, captions, media search, and export.
Official hosted MCP for posters, thumbnails, pitch decks, social variants, exports, and comments around the finished film.
OAuth-based YouTube upload and channel automation when the final cut is ready to ship.

title: Compare video and image models before spending the budget
summary: Run the same shot across model hubs and direct endpoints, then assemble a fair comparison reel with prompt, cost, and task IDs intact.
best_for: Directors and creative technologists choosing between Veo, Kling, Seedance, Runway, FLUX, and other fast-moving models for a specific look.
martini_handoff: Use Martini when the shootout becomes a production record: takes from every model side by side, with each keeper's model, prompt, references, and cost attached to the shot.

primary.why: Runs candidate models side by side on one canvas and records which model, prompt, and references produced each keeper.
Helps lint prompts, inspect pricing, and choose models with budget constraints in mind.
Hosted model schemas, uploads, job widgets, and video/image model routing.
Broad hosted access to image, video, audio, and voice models with async jobs.
Useful for browsing, pricing, and running a wide spread of media models through one MCP.
Direct Runware API route with schema validation, pricing, account balance, task lookup, and image/video/audio/3D tools.
Local FFmpeg-backed assembly for contact sheets, reels, captions, and QC.

title: Build a character-consistent series
summary: A route for recurring characters, locked references, episode state, and repeatable social or short-film production.
best_for: Episodic shorts, AI influencers, recurring product mascots, explainers, and social series.
martini_handoff: Use Martini when continuity must live in the same place as the generated takes and the cut: a Library of recurring characters, props, and locations, the timeline, and a record of how every shot was made.

primary.why: Library collections for recurring characters, props, and locations, shared across projects, plus the canvas and timeline where episodes are generated and cut.
Hosted video/image connector with character-consistency-oriented workflows.
Official image server for repeatable styles, raster/vector assets, upscaling, and background work.
Low-latency TTS, voice cloning, voice changing, infill, and localization.
Keeps characters, locations, shot status, and session orientation grounded in project files.
Hosted production database operations for episodes, assets, reviews, and status fields.

title: Edit local footage without handing over the source library
summary: A workstation-first path for agents that need to inspect, transcode, caption, cut, finish, and export media locally.
best_for: Editors, post teams, agencies with client footage, and productions where local media access matters.
martini_handoff: Use Martini only when the edit needs new generated shots or a shared timeline for review; keep purely local editorial work in local tools.

primary.why: Built around local agent-operated timeline editing, media search, captioning, and export.
Deep local Resolve Studio control for editing, grading, Fusion, and render workflows.
Local trim, concat, caption, QC, audio normalization, and repurposing operations.
Official transcription, diarization, and audio intelligence for editorial search and captions.
Official image enhancement/upscaling for stills, plates, and frames.

title: Turn an archive or dailies library into a trailer
summary: Search footage semantically, pull moments, assemble a trailer or cutdown, and publish reviewable versions.
best_for: Dailies, interviews, event footage, generated clip archives, and b-roll libraries.
martini_handoff: Use Martini if the archive cutdown needs newly generated inserts, team review on the shots, or XML back to Premiere or Resolve for finishing.

primary.why: Indexes, searches, summarizes, and analyzes video libraries for moment retrieval.
Frame.io review comments, shares, versions, uploads, metadata, and webhooks.
Hosted file search and access for governed Workspace footage folders.
Official hosted/local MCP for uploading, searching, transforming, archiving, and delivering image/video assets.
Agent-operable timeline editing and media search for trailer assembly.
Official video hosting, asset upload, playback IDs, analytics, and webhooks.

title: Create avatar, talking-head, or UGC-style video
summary: A route for product demos, explainers, digital twins, localized presenter videos, and lip-synced social spots.
best_for: Avatar explainers, founder-style ads, localized presenters, product walkthroughs, and high-volume social creative.
martini_handoff: Use Martini when avatar clips need to sit in a broader cut with generated B-roll, music, and edits, reviewed by the team and tracked for spend.

primary.why: Purpose-built for captioned, lip-synced UGC and social publishing from an agent.
Hosted avatar videos, lipsync, digital twins, voice library, and translation.
Official hosted MCP for D-ID API and docs around avatar video.
Comprehensive community MCP for replicas, personas, video generation, conversations, and lipsync.
Voice cloning, TTS, sound effects, and dialogue cleanup.

title: Generate voice, score, and sound assets
summary: A focused audio route for voiceover, dialogue patching, temp scores, sound effects, speech-to-speech, and localization.
best_for: Narration, ADR-style patches, temp music, sound effects, character voice tests, and localized deliverables.
martini_handoff: Use Martini when generated audio needs to stay attached to the shots and timeline it scores, alongside the approved video takes.

primary.why: Official server covering TTS, voice cloning, SFX, music, transcription, and audio isolation.
Low-latency TTS, STT, cloning, voice changing, infill, and localization.
Official MCP for lyrics, songs, instrumental music, and local playback.
Official transcription, diarization, audio intelligence, and TTS.
Audio post automation for leveling, noise reduction, loudness, and cleanup via Zapier.

title: Use only hosted remote MCP servers
summary: A cloud-agent-safe route for clients that can connect to hosted Streamable HTTP or SSE endpoints but cannot spawn local processes.
best_for: Web agents, locked-down sandboxes, demos, and automation where local binaries or desktop apps are unavailable.
martini_handoff: Use Martini as the hosted studio when the agent needs to move from tool discovery into coordinated production work: one remote MCP URL, or the CLI and API where the agent has a shell.

primary.why: One OAuth remote MCP endpoint for a full AI video production workspace: models, canvas, Library, timeline, and export.
Official hosted video generation endpoint for agent clients.
Hosted endpoint for running and chaining many image, video, audio, and voice models.
Hosted MCP for image/video models, schemas, uploads, and job widgets.
Hosted OAuth MCP for design generation, campaign assets, comments, and exports.
Hosted production tracking and schema-aware base operations.
Official remote file search, read, create, and governance-aware access.
Streamable HTTP endpoint for media uploads, search, transformations, archives, and CDN-ready asset delivery.

title: Run a hackable open film lab
summary: A mostly local and inspectable route for labs, students, R&D teams, and technical filmmakers who want workflows they can modify.
best_for: Local GPU experiments, open-source film labs, student projects, pipeline R&D, and teams that prize control over polish.
martini_handoff: Use Martini when a lab experiment graduates into a production that needs shared state, team review, spend accounting, and delivery pressure.

primary.why: Drive ComfyUI image, video, audio, and workflow graphs from Claude or ChatGPT.
Local workflow execution and graph control for inspectable generation pipelines.
The canonical Blender MCP for modeling, texturing, importing assets, and previz.
Guardrailed local video operations with FFmpeg, subtitles, QC, SFX, and repurposing.
Search and pull licensed sound assets into an agentic pipeline.

title: Transcribe dailies and caption the cut
summary: Transcription with speaker diarization, then add subtitles and captions as SRT or VTT files or burn them in, from hosted speech-to-text and local caption tools.
best_for: Interview and documentary transcripts, dialogue logging, subtitles for festival deliverables, closed captions, SRT and VTT export, and burned-in captions for social cuts.
martini_handoff: Martini is not needed for transcription or captions; use it only if the captioned cut is one the team is already generating and reviewing on a shared Martini timeline.

primary.why: Official Nova transcription with speaker diarization and audio intelligence, the strongest official cloud speech-to-text MCP.
Speaker-labelled and plain SRT/VTT subtitles across roughly a hundred source languages, with an exact quote a human approves first.
Hosted diarized transcription with word-level timestamps, plus speaker separation and denoise for messy location audio.
Local Kinocut video_subtitles burns captions into the file with FFmpeg, no upload and no credits.

title: Dub, translate and lip-sync for other languages
summary: Dubbing and translation of a finished cut: clone the original voice, translate the dialogue, dub the track and lip-sync the performer so the localized version keeps the take.
best_for: Localisation of a finished film or spot, AI dubbing into other languages, voice cloning for dubbed dialogue, lip sync on footage you shot, and translated subtitles alongside the dub.
martini_handoff: Martini is not needed for dubbing or localisation; use it only if the dubbed versions belong to a cut the team is already reviewing on a shared Martini timeline.

primary.why: Hosted video translation with lip-sync in 175+ languages, batches of up to 100, and voice cloning on the same OAuth connection.
Regenerates the performer's mouth on footage you already shot, with cost estimation before the render; the ADR and dub-pass tool.
Voice cloning, speech-to-speech and dubbing on the hosted endpoint, with Scribe transcription across 99 languages.
localize_voice and pronunciation dictionaries keep a character's invented names consistent across every language version.

title: Finish the master: upscale, grade, denoise and loudness
summary: The finishing pass on delivery masters: upscale to 4K, colour grade, denoise soft plates, and check loudness and true peak against broadcast and streaming specs.
best_for: Upscaling keeper frames and clips to 4K, color grading in Resolve, denoising generated footage that came out soft, and loudness normalization before delivery.
martini_handoff: Martini is not needed for finishing; use it only if the shots being upscaled already live on a Martini timeline and the team reviews them there, where upscale_assets quotes before it spends.

primary.why: Topaz Labs' own enhance and upscale models for stills, plates and frames; image only, so pair it with fal for video.
The practical MCP route to Topaz video upscaling (fal-ai/topaz/upscale/video) and other upscalers with no first-party server.
Official remote upscaler with relight and crop for plates; use explicit prompts for faithful enhancement rather than reinterpretation.
Resolve's colour page and render queue under agent control for the grade and the final export.
Integrated LUFS, true-peak and delivery-spec grading (EBU R128, streaming platforms) with the ffmpeg loudnorm fix returned.
Cloud upscale and denoise to 1080p/2K without a local GPU, billed by the second; a spot-fix tool for short clips.

title: Make a music video from a generated song
summary: Song generation first, then video shots generated to the track and cut to the beat: music video, lyric video and visualizer work where the audio drives the edit.
best_for: Music videos for a generated or licensed song, lyric videos, visualizers, artist promos, and cuts timed to the beat.
martini_handoff: Use Martini only when the video needs generated shots cut to the track on a shared timeline the artist or label reviews; the song itself comes from the music servers, not Martini.

primary.why: Official server for lyrics, full songs and instrumentals; a first-party alternative to Suno resellers with no licensing cloud.
Prompt or your own lyrics to a 60-180 second recording with vocals in eleven languages, one credit per take.
Hosted Gen-4.5, Seedance, Kling and Veo for performance and visual shots, with per-model ratios and durations from listModels.
Hosted roster with consistent-character training, so the same performer survives across every shot of the video.
Local Kinocut trim, merge, normalize and release checks to cut the shots to the track without a cloud render.

title: Break down the script and build storyboards and previz
summary: Script breakdown into scenes and a shot list, concept frames and storyboards, reference stills, and 3D previz before any generation credits are spent.
best_for: Screenplay breakdowns, shot lists, storyboard boards, concept art and keyframes, lookbooks and mood boards, location reference, and previs or 3D blocking of a scene.
martini_handoff: Martini is not needed for breakdowns, boards or previz; use it only when the boards are about to become generated shots the team reviews on one canvas.

primary.why: Parses a screenplay into a shot-by-shot breakdown and emits video-model prompts with cross-shot character consistency.
Official FLUX.2 stills and multi-reference composition for concept art, keyframes and start frames.
Official Miro MCP writes storyboard layouts and shot-planning walls as SVG boards the whole team can see.
Searches 5,489 films frame by frame by lighting, lens, shot size, colour and mood for lookbooks and shot references.
The most-adopted Blender MCP: build sets, place cameras and pull viewport screenshots for previz.

title: Animate stylised and anime characters from reference frames
summary: Stylised and animated characters: anime, illustration and cartoon looks held across shots with style references, character references and image-to-video from drawn keyframes.
best_for: Anime and cartoon shorts, illustrated or painterly looks, animated characters that must stay on-model, motion transfer onto drawn frames, and open-model LoRA pipelines.
martini_handoff: Martini is not needed for stylised animation; use it only if the animated shots are part of a cut the team reviews on a shared Martini timeline.

primary.why: create_image takes style, character and modify references and create_video pins frame0 and frame1, so a drawn look carries into motion.
Hosted Character Studio, Motion Transfer and Extend Video steps alongside Pika 2.5, Wan and Kling for stylised motion.
Kling's own hosted image-to-video on current models, the shortest route from an on-model still to a moving shot.
FLUX 3 keyframe animation and clip continuation from a FLUX.2 still, with a draft render before the full-quality pass.
Comfy Org's own server runs AnimateDiff, LTX and custom LoRA workflows on your GPU for looks hosted models cannot hold.

title: Publish, schedule and send out review links
summary: The last mile: YouTube upload, social cutdowns and scheduling across platforms, review and approval links for the client, hosting with analytics, and thumbnails.
best_for: YouTube and Vimeo publishing, scheduling shorts and social posts, client review links with timecoded comments, festival and press-kit hosting, and channel analytics after release.
martini_handoff: Martini is not needed for publishing; use it only to render or export the MP4 at the end of a Martini production, then hand that file to these servers.

primary.why: Still the only well-maintained MCP that does real YouTube uploads via OAuth, with metadata, playlists, captions and thumbnails.
Schedules and publishes to YouTube, Instagram, X, LinkedIn and Threads, with clip jobs that cut long footage into shorts.
Adobe's hosted Frame.io MCP: version stacks, review comments, share links and reviewers for client approval.
Pulls short clips from a long cut, captions and reframes them, then publishes or schedules to connected accounts.
Official Vimeo MCP for showcases, metadata, privacy, retention and geographic analytics after release.
Official Canva MCP for YouTube thumbnails, posters and social variants exported in delivery formats.

title: Turn a podcast or long talking recording into clips
summary: Repurpose long talking footage: pick the best moments into ranked clips, remove filler words, caption them, reframe to vertical shorts, and publish or schedule them.
best_for: Podcast episodes, interviews, webinars, panels and lectures that need highlight clips, shorts, captions and a publishing schedule without a manual edit.
martini_handoff: Martini is not needed for podcast repurposing; it is built for generated shots, and a clip pass over recorded talking footage has none.

primary.why: Ranks clips from a long file by virality score, pulls the word-timed transcript, fixes clips with named edit operations, then schedules them.
Prompt-driven moment detection, captions in 100+ languages, face-tracked 9:16 reframe and publishing to connected accounts.
Transcript-based editing with filler-word removal, Studio Sound, captions and highlight reels, published to a Descript link.
Kinocut's video_repurpose, caption burn-in and audio normalize run locally with receipts when the footage cannot leave the machine.

title: Make a short film with generated shots
summary: A narrative short from script to finished cut: a studio to hold the shots, video generation for coverage, directed dialogue and score, and an edit bay for the finish.
best_for: Narrative shorts, proof-of-concept scenes, festival pieces and pilots built from generated shots with recurring characters, dialogue, score and a real edit.
martini_handoff: Use Martini when the film is a sequence of generated shots the director reviews and cuts with the agent: Library continuity, provenance and spend per shot, and XML out to Resolve or Premiere for the finish. One generated clip does not need it.

primary.why: Shots, takes, Library characters and the multi-track timeline on one canvas the director and agent share, with XML export to Premiere, Resolve or Final Cut.
Hosted alternative that carries a script through storyboard, locked references, voiceover and shots to a cut MP4, aimed at long-form output.
Hosted first-party access to Gen-4.5, Seedance, Kling and Veo for coverage, with model-specific ratios and durations.
The most direct official route to Veo 3.1, with extension, first/last-frame and reference-to-video tools.
Octave performs lines with prompt-directed emotion and delivery, which is what narrative dialogue needs.
Voice cloning, sound effects, music and dialogue isolation from one official audio server.
video_to_music composes to the cut's pacing and cut points from a catalogue trained on licensed music.
Conform the timeline, grade and render in Resolve, the most actively maintained NLE MCP in the directory.
